skill.name: code-reviewer
skill.description: Review pull requests and codebases with structured checks for quality, security, maintainability, and team standards across common languages.
skill.summary: Reviews code with scripts, checklists, and security-focused guidance for common engineering stacks.

security_audit.summary: The only confirmed issues are three Python helper scripts that can write JSON reports to any user supplied output path. The Markdown code fences, reference links, anti-pattern headings, and .env template copy are false positives; no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or network behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Constrain --output to a safe report directory, warn before overwriting files, and reject sensitive paths such as shell profiles or environment files.
Label setup, Docker, and Kubernetes commands as optional examples that require user confirmation before execution.

content.user_title: Review Pull Requests with Structured Checks
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss security, maintainability, and testing issues when teams rely on memory alone. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured scripts and checklists for consistent review feedback.
actual_capabilities: Provides three Python helper scripts for pull request analysis, code quality checks, and report generation.
Validates that a target path exists before analysis starts.
Prints a simple review report with target, status, and finding count.
Can emit JSON results when the --json option is used.
Includes reference documents for review checklists, coding standards, and common antipatterns.
limitations: The scripts currently return placeholder findings rather than deep static analysis results.
The output file option can overwrite files if an unsafe path is supplied.
The references are broad templates and may need team-specific rules.
It does not integrate directly with GitHub, GitLab, or CI systems.

use_cases.title: Prepare Pull Request Feedback
use_cases.description: Run a structured review pass before submitting comments on a teammate's pull request.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Review Criteria
use_cases.description: Use the checklists to align reviews around quality, security, performance, and maintainability.

use_cases.title: Create Review Report Artifacts
use_cases.description: Generate simple text or JSON review summaries that can be shared during code quality discussions.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Review Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-reviewer skill to create a basic checklist for reviewing this pull request. Focus on correctness, tests, readability, and obvious security issues.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Local Quality Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-reviewer scripts against this project path and summarize the report in plain language. Ask before writing any output file.

prompt_templates.title: Review Against Team Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this change against the coding standards reference. List the highest priority review comments and explain why each one matters.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Risk-Focused Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a risk-focused review using the checklist, coding standards, and antipatterns references. Prioritize issues by impact, confidence, and required remediation.

output_examples.input: Review a small pull request that changes authentication middleware.
output: High priority: verify that authentication failures stop the request before protected handlers run.
Medium priority: add tests for expired tokens and missing credentials.
Low priority: simplify repeated error messages for easier maintenance.

output_examples.input: Generate a review summary for a service refactor.
output_examples.output: The review summary lists the target path, completion status, and number of findings. It then explains review concerns in concise human-readable language.

output_examples.input: Check a frontend change against code quality standards.
output: Confirm component state is scoped to the smallest practical owner.
Check that loading and error states are handled clearly.
Request tests for user-visible behavior instead of implementation details.

best_practices: Ask for confirmation before running commands that install packages, write files, or affect infrastructure.
Adapt the reference checklists to the project language, framework, and risk profile.
Review the generated findings manually before posting feedback to a pull request.
anti_patterns: Do not treat placeholder script findings as a complete static analysis result.
Do not write output files to sensitive paths or overwrite existing project files without approval.
Do not run deployment or Kubernetes examples during a code review unless the user explicitly requests it.

faq.question: Does this skill perform full static analysis?
faq.answer: No. The included scripts provide a basic framework and placeholder findings, so manual review is still required.

faq.question: Can it review multiple languages?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation targets common JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Swift, and Kotlin review concerns.

faq.question: Can it write reports to files?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts can write JSON output when --json and --output are used, but output paths should be reviewed first.

faq.question: Does it connect to GitHub or GitLab?
faq.answer: No. It runs as local scripts and reference guidance without direct repository platform integration.

faq.question: Is it safe to run infrastructure commands from the documentation?
faq.answer: Only run them after explicit approval. The Docker and Kubernetes commands are examples, not required review steps.

faq.question: How should teams customize it?
faq.answer: Teams should replace generic checklist items with project-specific security, testing, performance, and style requirements.
